bayts.text: The Everlasting (Al-Bāqī) has cured me of illnesses, and has overthrown whoever denied in opposition.
To Him my gratitude for my life, (lived as) a servant and a servitor, who has triumphed through the signs.
I thank Him with the gratitude of those who drank of His sweet water and were brought near to the Gardens.
I have won a life such as is not seen for others than me, a miracle made manifest by the leave of the Best.
The Munificent (Al-Jawād) bestows on me the finest steeds, and my request becomes compliant.
The Everlasting has given me life without causing me to die, without strife or gloating (of enemies).
The Everlasting has given me the mightiest Book, and I meet none who has grown arrogant.
On my behalf He has rewarded my mother and my father with abundant good that never ceases to endure.
He has benefited me, through the Chosen, the accepted Intercessor — upon him His two peaces —, with the benefit of the most beneficial.
My pens have called to gratitude toward Him Who has subjected creation to me, while I abide in safety.
My Lord is my Sovereign, my intimate and the Beloved, and He has already effaced from me the cause (to resort) to a physician.
He has cured me of every defect and illness, and led health to me in every aim.
I have been healed of the faults of my soul by taking refuge with Him Whose gates will never be shut.
He is the Generous, the Most Generous, the Honourer, and from Him generosity does not depart from me.
Muḥammad is my means of approach and my shield (junna) against every evil and harm, and my garden (janna).
There goes from me a peace, after a blessing, to him, with his Family and the most excellent of his company.
Our Messenger Aḥmad has raised all of me: upon him the best of the blessings of the Most High.
I have adorned for him virgin (unprecedented) praises among those who ignored my standing; and He has made the soul clear.
My heart has become clear through my Lord being my intimate, my beloved; and for me He has made my little abundance.
He has turned toward me the sweetness of the two Abodes, and in both He has made me protected (lit. "two neighbours").
He has benefited me with what appeared and what was hidden, and His being for me with my wishes has not been hidden.
I have rejoiced in Allah, the Generous, in the Messenger and his party, and I have obtained from Him the best of requests.
My gain is the praise of him through whom the Everlasting repelled a harm that headed for me, and it was repelled.
The Wise has made me an arbiter — and He is the Judge (Al-Ḥakam) — and from Him come to me wishes and wisdoms.
The All-Aware and the All-Knowing lead to me that beneath which lie the sciences and teaching.
The All-Aware has banished ignorance from my heart: I have become, through Him, worthy to spread knowledge.
The All-Knowing has freed me from error, and I have become just, without failing.
The Wise has effaced the trial that had befallen all my being: O, my gift has come!
To me has come the gift of the Generous, and all that I used to long for from Allah.
The verses of the Sender of the Book are my feast of welcome, and I am set apart from harm.
When I recite a verse I attain wishes from a Sovereign Who grants possession, Who has already given security.
The peace of an Everlasting One Who never ceases to be most generous (be) upon him who conveys generosity to me.
(Upon him) the two most lasting peaces of Him Who led to me, in exchange for everything, good pleasure, and it yielded.
A gift from me to the best of creation: may He Who guided and fashioned bless him.
Stretching my hand toward other than Him Who led wishes to me without harm, and made all of me secure,
I deem it, in travel and at home, among what contradicts the good pleasure of the Muḍarite (the Prophet).
To Allah, in the two Abodes, through al-Māḥī, (is stretched) my hand, bound to the greatest good pleasure.
To me my Lord, through the Chosen, has led all that I asked, with good pleasure, delivered.
My gift to the Chosen (is) forever, without toil, harm or hardship.
Whoever has thought that he could ever please him with what appeared like my service,
I have refuted his thought by my being the Servant (al-Khadīm), with that the like of which every servant fell short of.
That gladdened him — may Allah bless him — in the Family, the Companions and whoever befriends him.
The distress of whoever distressed me among the enemies — upon him (the Prophet) the two peaces of the Destroyer of aggressors —
(falls) upon everyone who distressed me before and did not repent: in this world and the Next, a fetter.
The Guide (Al-Hādī) has guided me by the standing of the guide (the Prophet), just as He accepted through him my striving (jihād).
My Lord has turned (toward me), according to the measure of the greatness of the Essence of the Generous, magnified favours.
He drives to me what I desire, without end or harm, just as in Him my journey has reached its end.
The Everlasting has driven to me a hospitality without cease: "Be!" and it is — for me He directs the aim.
(By) the honouring of Him Who has no end, the gifts hasten to me.
The bounty of the Generous has hastened to me and the generosity of an Everlasting, Loving One: I do not part from generosity.
God has willed that I be honoured, intimate and beloved, and through Him I am honoured.
I am well pleased with Him and He is well pleased with me (cf. Qurʾān 98:8), and He has been for me with security in my aims.
The Beautiful (Al-Jamīl) has come to meet me — how excellent! — with the beautiful, and toward other than what He chose for me I do not incline.
He has banished what He was not pleased with for me and veiled my secret and my fault, and has bought my wares.
